claims.text: A machine-learning-augmented free-energy protocol can replace full explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
Static ab initio calculations and short molecular-dynamics trajectories are sufficient to train an accurate interatomic potential for both solid and liquid phases.
The trained potential can capture anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling.
Elemental and simple binary systems near melting are the initial target domain.
CoCrFeNiTax is a multicomponent high-entropy-alloy system proposed for eventual extension of the method.
Training data should include static DFT calculations and sparse molecular-dynamics snapshots from both solid and liquid phases.
The machine-learning potential should include uncertainty estimates.
Thermodynamic integration or umbrella sampling over the learned potential can be used to calculate phase free energies and entropy contributions.
Additional chemical disorder is expected when the protocol is extended to multicomponent systems.
The accuracy of the learned free-energy surface, including the solid–liquid transition region, controls the fidelity of vibrational entropy and anharmonic effects.
Learning the high-dimensional potential-energy landscape from sparse ab initio data can reproduce the key features of solid and liquid phases.
Using the learned surrogate reduces the number of costly full ab initio molecular-dynamics steps.
Free-energy integration over the learned landscape retains important entropy and anharmonic contributions.
The protocol will reduce computational cost by approximately one order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
For elemental and binary systems, the protocol will have fidelity at least comparable to TOR-TILD.
Accuracy may decrease for complex multicomponent high-entropy systems.
The protocol is validated for elemental and binary alloys near their fusion temperatures.
Its performance in multicomponent high-entropy systems remains unconfirmed.
There is uncertainty about whether the model can reliably capture electron–vibration coupling and anharmonic effects across diverse chemistries.
Deviation of phase free energies or derived observables by more than 5–10% from explicit ab initio MD and TOR-TILD results would falsify the replacement hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions describe elemental and binary evaluations as initial tests to be performed, whereas the boundary states that the method is already validated for those systems.
